criterion_notes.c1: Examines household drinking-water service access in Spain, specifically water affordability and supply disconnections (cuts) for non-payment among families at risk of poverty and social exclusion.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, it examines international, national, regional, and municipal legal and regulatory frameworks for household water supply. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it directly analyzes rule-type mechanisms governing service access: statutory minimum vital supply guarantees (e.g., Cantabria and Catalonia laws), municipal tariff bonuses/discounts and social funds, administrative eligibility rules (household unemployment, income thresholds, no prior arrears, habitual residence, annual renewal), legal classification of charges as public fees (tasas collected via administrative apremio) versus private prices under outsourced management, and municipal rules/exceptions governing suspension of water supply for non-payment.
criterion_notes.c3: Fails Criterion 3 (E05). The authors explicitly describe the work as a critical normative essay ('este ensayo que se apoya en un análisis crítico de la garantía del derecho humano al agua desde una perspectiva normativa') aimed at proposing legal reform. It contains no empirical methodology, no primary quantitative or qualitative data collection, no systematic empirical synthesis, and no empirical case-study design; it relies solely on doctrinal review of statutes/case law and narrative citation of secondary descriptive statistics from industry associations (AEAS, AEOPAS), the national statistics institute (INE), and an ombudsman report.
criterion_notes.c4: No empirical study outcome is measured or evaluated. Although the essay discusses household water affordability and supply disconnections conceptually and cites aggregate secondary descriptive estimates from industry reports (e.g., AEOPAS and AEAS figures on annual residential supply cuts and social measure coverage), it conducts no empirical outcome assessment.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails Criterion 5 because there is no empirical sample, unit-of-analysis dataset, or identifiable empirical study design linking exposure and outcome—the paper is a normative/doctrinal legal essay and narrative policy overview.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English and Spanish title, abstract, and keywords. Per Criterion 10, comprehension/translation directly from the provided Spanish full text is fully feasible (assessed directly by bilingual AI screener), though the record is excluded under E05 for lack of empirical evidence.

evidence_quotes.quote: In this essay, based on a critical approach, the protection of the human right of access to water in Spain is analysed against situations of risk of poverty and social exclusion to propose a legal reform.
Precisamente, el debate sobre la pobreza hídrica en España motiva este ensayo que se apoya en un análisis crítico de la garantía del derecho humano al agua desde una perspectiva normativa.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 6 of 12 (Medidas de acción social clásicas: Bonificaciones y descuentos en la tarifa, p. 108)
evidence_quotes.quote: Los criterios de acceso, la cuantía y el modo de aplicación de los descuentos y bonificaciones por razones de renta son establecidos siguiendo los criterios de cada municipio, de modo que la dispersión competencial da por resultado un diseño muy heterogéneo a lo largo de todo el territorio nacional

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 7 of 12 (Excepciones municipales al corte del suministro por impago, p. 109)
evidence_quotes.quote: Los reglamentos u ordenanzas municipales reguladoras del suministro de agua potable a domicilio contemplan como obligación del abonado el pago de las facturas emitidas en contraprestación por el servicio, de modo que el impago de las mismas es causa de la suspensión del suministro.

Por tanto, es una realidad innegable que los cortes de suministro existen en España, pero no es posible determinar con precisión cuántos de ellos pueden estar relacionados con la incapacidad de las familias en riesgo de pobreza y exclusión social para hacer frente a la contraprestación económica por el servicio urbano de aguas

raw_response.exposure: National, regional (autonomous community), and municipal legal and regulatory rules in Spain governing household drinking-water supply, tariff discounts/bonuses, social funds, eligibility requirements, and supply disconnections for non-payment
raw_response.outcome: Household drinking-water affordability and protection against supply disconnection for non-payment (discussed normatively with secondary descriptive industry estimates; no empirical outcome evaluation)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Families / households at risk of poverty and social exclusion in Spain (discussed conceptually; no empirical study sample)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). While the paper squarely addresses household drinking-water affordability and disconnections (c1) and analyzes specific statutory and municipal rule-type mechanisms governing tariff discounts, social funds, eligibility screening, and disconnection prohibitions (c2, satisfying both plain and narrow 2026-10-13 readings), it is explicitly a critical normative legal essay ('ensayo ... desde una perspectiva normativa') proposing legal reform. It presents no primary empirical data, no qualitative or quantitative empirical methods, and no systematic empirical synthesis, relying only on doctrinal analysis of legal texts and narrative citation of secondary industry reports.
raw_response.study_design: Normative and doctrinal legal analysis / critical policy essay (non-empirical)
